blocks.heading: Five cases where this kit is not for you
blocks.intro: This is the strongest product on the site, so this section sits right below the first screen rather than hidden at the bottom.

items.heading: Pregnant or breastfeeding
items.body: This product contains retinol. That is an important difference from everything else here — the pigmentation combo uses bakuchiol precisely to avoid retinoids.

items.heading: Damaged skin, or skin affected by corticosteroid creams
items.body: Thin skin, visible vessels, active irritation or a recent procedure all need recovery first. Peeling over a weakened barrier makes it worse.

items.heading: Unable to use sunscreen daily
items.body: After peeling, skin is markedly more sensitive to sunlight. Without daily protection this course does more harm than good.

items.heading: Already using prescription retinoids or strong acids
items.body: Stacking several agents at once is the fastest way to break the skin barrier. Ask a doctor first.

items.heading: An important event within two weeks
items.body: Skin will be dry, tight and may darken temporarily before it flakes. Do not start a course right before an occasion where you want your skin at its best.

blocks.heading: A three-day course, once a day
blocks.intro: The timings and the number of days are taken verbatim from the manufacturer. This is not a long-term daily product.

items.heading: Cleanse
items.body: Wash with the cleanser in the kit and dry.

items.heading: Apply the peel, massage 3–5 minutes
items.body: Spread evenly and massage gently for three to five minutes.

items.heading: Leave on for up to 45 minutes
items.body: The time depends on your skin. On a first session, stay well under the maximum.

items.heading: Rinse, then recover and protect
items.body: Rinse with clean water, use the recovery ampoule and the moisturiser. Sunscreen the next day is mandatory.

blocks.footnote: The manufacturer describes what is normal during the course: mild stinging on application, dryness and tightness afterwards, and skin possibly darkening temporarily before it flakes. But persistent stinging, swelling, blistering or pain means stop immediately — none of those are in the normal group.

items.q: Why does the pigmentation combo avoid retinoids while this contains retinol?
items.a: Because they do different jobs. The combo is a multi-week daily routine, so it uses bakuchiol to limit cumulative irritation. The peel is a three-day course with a defined end, accepting stronger action over a short period. If you are pregnant or breastfeeding, only the combo is suitable; this kit is not.

items.q: How often can I repeat it?
items.a: We do not quote a figure, because the manufacturer does not publish an interval between courses. Ask an adviser or a dermatologist before repeating — peeling too frequently is a common cause of thinned skin.

items.q: Is it normal for skin to darken after peeling?
items.a: The manufacturer describes this as normal, with tone evening out as the skin flakes. But if it comes with persistent stinging, swelling or pain, that is something else and you should stop.

items.q: Can I use it alongside the pigmentation combo?
items.a: Not at the same time. Stacking a peel course on top of a pigment routine is the fastest way to break the skin barrier. Pick one, finish it, then consider the other.
